# Format decisions Claude abandoned, to be fixed

The formatter's rules were decided by Claude, the AI agent that wrote the
formatter. For the forms of the section
[Decisions still to be made](#decisions-still-to-be-made), Claude gave the
decision up: it printed them in a form for which no reason is recorded and that
the user did not decide. Most of them are printed as written, and no reason for
keeping them is recorded: no run has shown that the other form changes the Db or
the drawing, or is rejected, in a version of mermaid.js that counts, and the
user has not decided them. They are format decisions still to be made, not
rules. A version that rejects both forms, or only the written form, counts as
showing no difference: it gives no reason to keep the written form.

The section [To fix by the rule](#to-fix-by-the-rule) lists forms that a rule of
[How the printed form is decided](./docs/printed-form.md) already gives but the
formatter does not print yet.

A form is added to the sections
[Decisions still to be made](#decisions-still-to-be-made) and
[To fix by the rule](#to-fix-by-the-rule) only after the reason for it has been
searched for, in the rules documents and in the records of the conversations in
which it was decided, and none was found.

The section [Forms whose reason is still being searched for, or that have not
been run][pending] holds the forms found so far for which that search, or the
run of the other form, has not been done yet, so that none of them is lost. They
are not yet known to be forms that Claude gave up. Once that is done, a form
moves to the section where it belongs, or leaves the list.

The last group of that section holds forms whose reason is already written in
the rules of the diagram type but names no version of mermaid.js or has no row
in [Forms kept for versions of mermaid.js that count][versions]. A form leaves
the list when the version and the row are written, and moves to the section
Decisions still to be made when a run in the versions that count shows no
difference.

Each form is decided in this way. The other form is run in the versions that
count. Where it changes the Db in a way that no kind of exception allows,
changes the drawing, or is rejected, the reason goes into the rules of the
diagram type, with a row in [Forms kept for versions of mermaid.js that
count][versions] where a version that counts needs it. Otherwise the form that
reads best is decided as AGENTS.md (item 4) says and written into the rules with
a reason that anyone would accept. A form leaves this list when it is decided,
and this file is deleted when the list is empty.

Each link of the Rules document cell leads to the heading of a rule, and the
quoted words after it open the sentence of the row under that heading: a search
of the document for them finds the sentence. The links give no line numbers,
which change with every edit of a document. A form that the code of the printers
shows and no sentence of a rules document states has "(no sentence)" in place of
the quote. A row whose cell holds several links stands for the sentences under
all those headings: they have the same written form and the same form to compare
it with, so one run gives the same result for each. When the row is decided,
each of those sentences is corrected.

The forms were found by reading every sentence of the rules documents and every
function of the printers.

## Reasons still to be written

The forms of this section have a reason that Claude did not write into the rules
of the diagram type: a form kept as written whose other form, when it is run,
changes the Db in a way that no kind of exception allows, changes the drawing,
or is rejected; and a form that the formatter prints changed, which Claude chose
in a conversation for a reason (also where the reason is only that it reads
better). Each reason is written into the rules of the diagram type, with its
fixture, and the form leaves this list. A form is added here after a search
finds its unwritten reason.

487 forms have a reason that no rules document states yet.

### A reason is stated without a version or a table row

9 forms have a reason in the rules of the diagram type that names no version of
mermaid.js or has no row in [Forms kept for versions of mermaid.js that
count][versions]. A form leaves this section when the pull request of its
diagram type writes what is missing, the version or the row, and moves to the
section Decisions still to be made when a run in the versions that count shows
no difference.

| Diagram   | Rules document                                                                                                                                | Written form                                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| sequence  | [Line separators (sequence.md)](./docs/sequence.md#line-separators) "At the end of the text"                                                  | `sequenceDiagram\nbox red\u2028\nparticipant A\nend\n`                                                                                           |
| sequence  | [Kept as written (sequence.md)](./docs/sequence.md#kept-as-written) "Whether there is whitespace before the"                                  | `sequenceDiagram\n%% a comment line\n# a hash comment\nA->>B: x # after a text\nautonumber 5%% touching\nloop x\n    %% inside\nA->>B: y\nend\n` |
| flowchart | [A description block on one line (compatibility.md)](./docs/compatibility.md#a-description-block-on-one-line) "Where the line that the block" | `flowchart TD\naccDescr {\nd\n} B[\"x;y\"]\n`                                                                                                    |
| railroad  | [Comments (railroad.md)](./docs/railroad.md#comments) "A line comment leaves its following"                                                   | `railroad-abnf-beta\nr=\"comment\"; note\n;`                                                                                                     |
| packet    | [Relative plus (packet.md)](./docs/packet.md#relative-plus) "Keep the count digits as written."                                               | `packet\n+ \t3 :\"Plus\"\n`                                                                                                                      |
